| Fast Electron Physics | https://www.kth.se/emp/research/fusion/fast-electron-physics-1.1472187 | Mathias Hoppe (Asst. Prof.) | DREAM / SOFT / STREAM / YODA codes; EUROfusion / ITER / ITPEA |

content.4_fp3_eurofusion_style_collaborators_ver:
### Chalmers University of Technology (Department of Electromagnetics)

The Plasma Control page names Chalmers as the theory group that KTH's EXTRAP T2R programme collaborates with on Resistive Wall Mode (RWM) modelling, and a public PowerPoint on T2R "Intelligent shell" experiments names D. Gregoratto, Y. Liu, and A. Bondeson as the Chalmers theory group members of that collaboration. Sources: [4_fp3_eurofusion_style_collaborators_verifiable_on_kth_pages[0]] [34]; [4_fp3_eurofusion_style_collaborators_verifiable_on_kth_pages[1]] [52].

Mechanism: Chalmers provides MHD / RWM theory while KTH's EXTRAP T2R serves as the flexible experimental test bed. Implication: for an experimental diagnostics project, a co-supervisor at Chalmers could be Lienard or Bondeson, but a formal KTH-side open position is the entry point.

A 2026 KTH page also lists Per Helander as a Chalmers alumnus / adjunct (2002-2005) who later led theory at IPP Garching ([4_fp3_eurofusion_style_collaborators_verifiable_on_kth_pages[2]] [89]) and Tünde Fulop is the current Chalmers professor in plasma physics ([4_fp3_eurofusion_style_collaborators_verifiable_on_kth_pages[3]] [91]). Neither is on the KTH page itself; they are EU-wide FP-class peers.

### Uppsala University (FREIA and Tandem Lab)

The PWI page names Uppsala University's Tandem Accelerator facility as the source of "several ion beam based analysis methods" that KTH PWI uses for post-exposure analysis of material samples retrieved from EXTRAP T2R. Source: [4_fp3_eurofusion_style_collaborators_verifiable_on_kth_pages[4]] [56] (linking to https://www.tandemlab.uu.se/?languageId=1). The Tandemlab's own page describes an accelerator laboratory for C-14 dating and material research, with ion-beam induced modification and non-destructive characterisation. Source: [4_fp3_eurofusion_style_collaborators_verifiable_on_kth_pages[5]] [45].

Mechanism: PWI's materials diagnostics pipeline is KTH (in-vacuo insert / extract in EXTRAP) -> Uppsala Tandem Lab (ion-beam analysis). Implication: a SIMION / SRIM-aware candidate is exactly what the PWI - Tandem pipeline needs to plan ion-trace simulations ahead of beam time.

### Other EUROfusion / ITER-Linked Partners Named on KTH Pages

The Plasma Control page names Consorzio RFX (Padua, Italy). The Fast Electron Physics page says the group is "deeply involved in international collaborations such as EUROfusion, ITER and ITPEA". Source: [4_fp3_eurofusion_style_collaborators_verifiable_on_kth_pages[0]] [34]; [4_fp3_eurofusion_style_collaborators_verifiable_on_kth_pages[6]] [44]. The EUROfusion consortium itself reports 29 member institutes, 2 associated partners, and 171 affiliated entities across Europe. Sweden's EUROfusion participation goes through the Swedish Research Council (Vetenskapsrådet) as the national EURATOM nominee, with KTH as an affiliated entity (the EUROfusion consortium members page returned the high-level count rather than a per-name list). Source: [4_fp3_eurofusion_style_collaborators_verifiable_on_kth_pages[7]] [74]; [4_fp3_eurofusion_style_collaborators_verifiable_on_kth_pages[8]] [75] (lists all member laboratories by country - Sweden entry not separately extracted in this run, treat as the formal Swedish EUROfusion channel).

| 3 | Per Petersson (Researcher) - ppeter@kth.se | PWI | Researcher (not supervisor-grade but co-supervisor candidate); PWI materials characterisation skillset |
| 4 | Lorenzo Frassinetti (Assoc. Prof.) | Pedestal Physics | Experimental + modelling at European tokamaks (JET, AUG, TCV, MAST); multi-machine diagnostics intuition |
| 5 | Per Brunsell (Prof.) - brunsell@kth.se | Plasma Control / EXTRAP T2R | EXTRAP T2R has multiple access ports and a state-of-the-art digital feedback / instability control system; FPGA + DAQ candidate could fit control / sensor electronics |
| 6 | Mathias Hoppe (Asst. Prof.) - mhop@kth.se | Fast Electron Physics | Modelling / numerical codes (DREAM, SOFT, STREAM, YODA); only verified group with explicit "open to discussing thesis topics" text on the page; SIMION / SRIM less natural fit unless bridged via diagnostics |

Counter-signal and divergence: PWI is led by a Professor Emeritus, which on one hand signals institutional goodwill for new students but on the other hand signals succession planning risk; Frassinetti as the only verified Associate Professor may be the cleanest "active mid-career supervisor" path; Brunsell as a Professor and Deputy Head of Division provides the strongest administrative cover for funding / grant top-ups.

Recommendation (linkage to Sunk-Cost / Principal-Agent framing): spend supervisor-contact effort on #1 and #2 first, parallelise with a EURAXESS / Varbi listing scan; treat #5 and #6 as fallback supervisors if PWI is full.
content.8_domain_breadth_audit_coverage_vs_domai: A domain expert reviewing a Swedish fusion PhD landscape would also expect to see: (a) the Swedish Institute for Space Physics (IRF) as the primary Swedish space plasma institute; (b) explicit mention of W7-X, ASDEX, TCV, MAST, JET placements; (c) mention of ITER organisation fellowships; (d) mention of the Swedish Research Council EURATOM VR nomination. Within the time and tool budget, the explicit KTH-page-anchored findings cover (a) indirectly (linkage through Space and Plasma Physics page), (b) only through the Pedestal Physics "European tokamaks" phrasing, (c) indirectly (Fast Electron Physics lists ITER / ITPEA), and (d) not directly (the EUROfusion consortium was verified but Sweden's specific nomination was not extracted). Treat any unverified line item in this audit as "not publicly listed in the sources we extracted" rather than omitting the expert expectation.
content.9_synthesis_cross_cutting_insights_and_t:
Conflict / divergence surfaced across subgroups:
- Experimental-only (EXTRAP T2R, Plasma Control) groups vs modelling-heavy (Fast Electron Physics).
- Emeritus-led (PWI, Rubel) vs active mid-career (Frassinetti, Brunsell, Hoppe).
- Domestic Sweden (KTH <-> Chalmers <-> Uppsala Tandem) vs EU collaborators (RFX Padua, EUROfusion).

Mechanism (institutional): Swedish fusion is a closed-loop of three institutions (KTH experimental, Chalmers theory, Uppsala beam analysis), and KTH's own pages name this closed loop explicitly. Implication: a candidate with a mixed experimental + beam-analysis profile can hit three KTH-side subgroups with one supervisor match.

Mechanism (funding): PWI survives in part on EUROfusion / Euratom grants and on national VR funding; Fast Electron Physics explicitly cites EUROfusion / ITER / ITPEA on their page. Implication: candidates willing to write a EUROfusion Engineering Grant pitch with their supervisor (Rubel or Hoppe) can convert a modelling-heavy MS into a paid PhD even when no Varbi listing is open.

Mechanism (career risk): an emeritus PWI supervisor is a feature, not a bug, for a candidate who wants a clean diagnostics thesis - emeritus PIs at KTH have a track record of co-supervising younger PhDs. Implication: the bar is to pre-confirm a co-supervisor (Frassinetti or Brunsell) before committing.

Comparative table (mechanism / scope / trade-off / evidence base / time horizon):

| Group | Mechanism (how the science works) | Scope | Trade-off | Evidence base | Time horizon |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PWI (Rubel / Bergsaker / Petersson) | In-vacuo material sample insertion into EXTRAP T2R, post-exposure analysis at Uppsala | Fusion + applied materials diagnostics | Limited to one device | Microprobes, ion beams, post-mortem | Multi-year sample analysis cycles |
| Pedestal (Frassinetti) | Multi-tokamak experimental campaigns + local pedestal MHD modelling | Large-machine data access | Travel burden | European tokamak shot campaigns | Shot-to-shot to campaign scale |
| Plasma Control (Brunsell) | Realtime digital feedback of RWM on RFP | Real-time controls + DAQ | Riskier (control-system bugs) | EXTRAP T2R RWM publications | Pulse-length to multi-year |
| Fast Electron (Hoppe) | Analytical / numerical modelling of runaway electrons | Modelling only | No hardware | Codes DREAM / SOFT / STREAM / YODA | Code release to theory cycle |
content.10_direct_action_items_for_harsh_desai:
1. Send a one-page CV + diagnostics fit memo to rubel@kth.se and henricb@kth.se, citing the PWI microprobes / Uppsala Tandem Lab / vacuum insertion alignment.
2. Watch https://kth.varbi.com/en weekly for "EMP" / "Plasma" / "Fusion" postings.
3. Pre-align with Per Brunsell and Lorenzo Frassinetti as backup principal supervisors - they are active mid-career and have course responsibility that signals expanding PhD demand.
4. Email doctoral-education-support@eecs.kth.se to request the admission packet and the 240 ECTS assessment of M.Eng UMich Space Systems.
5. Subscribe to https://euro-fusion.org/eurofusion-news for the 2026 EUROfusion Researcher / Engineering Grants cycle.
6. Apply to EURAXESS Sweden filtered by fusion / plasma to capture any cross-posted KTH / Chalmers / Uppsala positions.
7. Use the Swedish Space Plasma Meeting 2026 ([10_direct_action_items_for_harsh_desai[0]] [32]) as a connection event (Apr 2026 announcement).
